objective.summary: Reduce or eliminate removable Partial declarations by moving real workflow, mutable state, persistence, validation, or presentation policy into existing concrete responsibility owners, while preserving XAML/public contracts, native lifetime, disposal order, and behavior.
constraints: Work only in C:\Git\2D\Dev; keep C:\Git\2D\Original read-only.
Do not mechanically merge, delete, rename, or move Partial files by line count.
Reuse existing concrete ViewModel, Presenter, Controller, adapter, service, or test owner before adding any new type.
Do not add one-implementation interfaces, managers, providers, factories, forwarding wrappers, or new manual Partials without an independently owned state/lifetime/test seam.
Generated XAML/designer/native composition and test-host Partials may remain only with explicit compile, binding, lifetime, or test-contract proof.
Preserve XAML names, public constructors, Recipe/XML behavior, Preview/Run behavior, image ownership, cancellation, shutdown, and PropertyGrid contracts.
One heartbeat run may change one independently verifiable Partial boundary only; do not wait for optional user input or hardware.
Do not commit, push, tag, release, deploy, or modify C:\Git\2D\Original from scheduled work.

criteria.text: All 59 current Partial declarations have a current owner, intended owner or retained reason, caller path, mutable-state writer, lifetime/release owner, and binding/public/test contract recorded against current source.
Each reviewed manual Partial with an independently owned responsibility is moved to an existing concrete owner, and the former Partial no longer owns that responsibility or direct coupling.

Any remaining generated, XAML, designer, native, or test Partial has an explicit reason that removal would break a framework/public/binding/lifetime/test contract, with no unreviewed business policy left in the retained declaration.
Every extraction slice passes a focused source contract, relevant build/test, forbidden-coupling search, and diff check while preserving existing observable behavior.

The final audit, documentation index, Solution Debug/Release builds, relevant smoke contracts, issue ledger, and owner/navigation documents pass; actual WPF runtime, hardware, GPU/SDK, and long-running native limits are recorded separately as unverified when not run.

events.summary: Open a new bounded issue instead of reopening resolved PL-0027. Treat the 59 declarations as candidates for real owner extraction; do not promise mechanical elimination of framework-required Partial composition.

For the first PL-0028 slice, reuse the existing Learn Presenter pattern and add one concrete ColorHsvLearnPresenter because OpenVisionLearnWindow owned animation state and HSV guide policy alongside WPF control projection. Keep the Window partial for XAML and move only independently testable state/text decisions.

Delete OpenVisionRecipeBasicLifecycleView.xaml.cs because it contained only the framework initialization constructor and the XAML has no control event or view-specific behavior. Preserve the compiled x:Class contract and verify through the existing Shell Recipe lifecycle contract and Debug/Release builds.

Delete OpenVisionRecipeValidationSuiteView.xaml.cs because it contained only the framework initialization constructor and the XAML contains command bindings without view event, DataContext, persistence, or inspection policy. Preserve its inherited Shell DataContext and validate the existing validation-suite contract plus Debug/Release builds.

Delete OpenVisionWorkspaceSamplePickerView.xaml.cs because it contained only the framework initialization constructor and the XAML contains bindings and styles without view event, DataContext, persistence, or inspection policy. Preserve the SamplePicker Window composition, Shell command caller, and ViewModel-owned state. Update the existing readiness source-layout expectation for the prior ColorHsvLearnPresenter owner so the focused contract remains current.

Retain OpenVisionShellHostWindow.xaml.cs as the concrete WPF composition and lifetime owner. It creates OpenVisionShellHostView, owns HWND hook registration/removal and responsive Window scaling, exposes startup/smoke projections consumed by multiple callers, and disposes the Shell on close. Moving these responsibilities into a new wrapper or manager would hide the Window boundary and add no independent owner or test seam.

Retain OpenVisionPendingToolView.xaml.cs as a narrow WPF adapter. Its only manual behavior injects the existing OpenVisionPendingToolViewModel into DataContext and exposes the same instance for composition; state, language events, and Dispose belong to the ViewModel and OpenVisionShellHostDocumentController. Removing the Partial or adding a wrapper would break the XAML constructor/composition contract without creating an independent owner.

Retain OpenVisionLayerDockWorkspaceView.xaml.cs as the concrete WPF/AvalonDock visual adapter. Its DependencyProperties, native DockingManager event bridge, guide/geometry methods, visual snapshots, and header diagnostics are directly consumed by existing docking composition/controllers. Moving them would either break the public visual contract or add a wrapper around the same control state without an independent lifetime or test seam.

Retain OpenVisionLayerDockingGuideOverlayView.xaml.cs as the concrete XAML visual adapter for docking guide zones. It owns the generated namescope, active-zone visibility and brush state, guide-zone count, and pane margin projection, while OpenVisionLayerDockWorkspaceView is the existing composition caller. Moving these operations would only wrap the same control state without an independent owner, lifetime, or test seam.

Retain ImageCanvasControl.cs and ImageCanvasControl.designer.cs as one concrete SharpGL/WinForms native rendering and lifetime boundary. The designer Partial creates the OpenGLControl and generated disposal wiring, while the main Partial owns rendering, input event subscriptions, P/Invoke, texture/overlay state, and ReleaseOpenGlControl. Moving either side would split the same native lifetime without an independent owner or test seam.
